resources.string: Set up and launch Linux, EmulationStation and PortMaster

Run a Linux system on your console alongside andr36oid. dArkOSen includes EmulationStation and PortMaster. Copy your ports to the games card, play them in the subsystem, then exit to return to Android.

This runs a Linux rootfs, such as dArkOSen, in a separate contained environment, a bit like Docker. With full handoff, Android\'s heavy background services are stopped first, so all of your open Android apps are closed while it runs. Speed should be close to running dArkOSen on its own hardware, but it uses the andr36oid kernel, so a few things may not behave exactly as expected. Your EASYROMS partition, or the data partition if you chose not to create EASYROMS, is mounted inside the Linux system as /roms.

Boot the rootfs to start Linux the way it normally runs, or launch EmulationStation or the included PortMaster directly. These launches use the automatically detected image. A full handoff gives Linux the screen and closes your Android apps. Save your work before launching.\n\nUse Setup steps to prepare your games card, or Advanced mode for other Linux images and a live boot console. Choose what starts at boot in Android Settings > System > Boot into the subsystem by default.
Never update dArkOSen from inside it

dArkOSen is running as a guest on top of andr36oid, not on its own hardware. Its built-in updater and upgrade scripts expect to own the whole device, so they are not safe here. If you run them from inside dArkOSen, they write to the wrong places and can destroy the dArkOSen install, or even corrupt your Android system and leave the console unable to boot.

Do not use any Update, Upgrade, or online-update option inside dArkOSen, EmulationStation, or PortMaster.

To update dArkOSen safely, exit to Android, power off, and replace the dArkOSen .img file on the storage partition with the new version. That is the only supported way to update.
I understand, and I will not update dArkOSen from inside it.

You can complete setup entirely offline. Copy an extracted .img file using a computer, insert the card, then choose Check again. A download is offered only when this device has an Internet connection.
dArkOSen already includes PortMaster. You only need to copy your ports to the games card. This wizard checks for a rootfs image; it does not verify your ports.

Your Linux image has been found. Finish setup to boot the rootfs, or launch EmulationStation or PortMaster directly.\n\nWith full handoff, launching closes Android apps and hands the display to Linux. Save your Android work first. Exit Linux to return to Android.

Once a Linux image is found, choose what starts at boot in Android Settings > System > Boot into the subsystem by default. Choose EmulationStation or PortMaster as the default target there. Use Advanced mode here to choose an image or change how Linux shares the console with Android.
Boot into the subsystem by default
Choose Android or Linux at startup, and the Linux app to open
Your console will start in the Linux subsystem. Hold START while it powers on to boot Android instead.
Your console will start in Android. Hold START while it powers on to boot the Linux subsystem instead.

Native init boot is experimental. It boots the image\'s own startup instead of launching a frontend directly, the way the firmware boots on its own hardware. Some images, including dArkOSen, may fail to take over the display and leave the screen black. If that happens, hold the power button to force a restart. Use a normal launch unless you are testing this.
Could not save the setting. Try again.

Choose a compatible Linux rootfs image and how it shares the console with Android. Other images must support the andr36oid kernel and this subsystem.\n\nKeep Android running to inspect the boot log without giving Linux the screen. This is useful for troubleshooting; graphical Linux apps may require full handoff.
Linux will take over the display. Android background services will stop and your open Android apps will close. Save your work before continuing. Exit Linux to return to Android.
Android stays on screen. Launch to watch the live Linux boot console. This mode does not hand the display to graphical Linux apps.
